15/**
16 * Core math backend interface for C-Kernel-Engine.
17 *
18 * This is intentionally minimal and matches the conventions already used
19 * in C-Transformer for GEMM kernels.
20 *
21 * Layout assumptions (LLM-style shapes):
22 * - A: [M x K], row-major, A(i,k) = A[i*K + k]
23 * - B: [N x K], row-major, B(j,k) = B[j*K + k]
24 * - C: [M x N], row-major, C(i,j) = C[i*N + j]
25 * - bias: optional [N], added per output column j
26 */
27typedef struct {
28 void (*sgemm)(int M, int N, int K,
29 const float *A, int lda,
30 const float *B, int ldb,
31 const float *bias,
32 float *C, int ldc);
33} CKMathBackend;

610// Fused GEMM + SwiGLU (LLaMA/SmolLM MLP gate+up projection)
611// Computes: output = SiLU(x @ W_gate + b_gate) * (x @ W_up + b_up)
612// Two GEMMs + SwiGLU fused into one pass - intermediates stay in registers
613void gemm_swiglu_fused(const float *x,
614 const float *W_gate,
615 const float *W_up,
616 const float *b_gate, // can be NULL
617 const float *b_up, // can be NULL
618 float *output,
619 int M, int N, int K);
620
621// =============================================================================
622// Fully Fused MLP Decode Kernels (T=1 token generation)
623// =============================================================================
624// These kernels fuse the ENTIRE MLP block: Gate + Up + SwiGLU + Down
625// Key benefit: Intermediate swiglu values stay in L1/L2, never touch DRAM
626// Target: AVX-512 / Intel Xeon 5th Gen (Sapphire/Emerald Rapids)
627
628// Version 1: Tiled fusion with thread-local accumulators
629// Best for: Small number of cores, when critical section overhead is low
630void fused_mlp_swiglu_decode(
631 const float *x, // [D] input
632 const float *W_gate, // [Hff, D] gate projection
633 const float *W_up, // [Hff, D] up projection
634 const float *W_down, // [D, Hff] down projection
635 const float *b_gate, // [Hff] or NULL
636 const float *b_up, // [Hff] or NULL
637 const float *b_down, // [D] or NULL
638 float *output, // [D] output
639 int D, // hidden dimension
640 int Hff); // intermediate dimension
641
642// Version 2: Two-phase (swiglu then down projection)
643// Best for: Many cores (24+), avoids critical section, better parallelism
644void fused_mlp_swiglu_decode_v2(
645 const float *x,
646 const float *W_gate,
647 const float *W_up,
648 const float *W_down,
649 const float *b_gate,
650 const float *b_up,
651 const float *b_down,
652 float *output,
653 int D,
654 int Hff);
655
656// Version 3: Tiled with atomic accumulation
657// Best for: Large L2 cache (2MB+), good cache reuse
658void fused_mlp_swiglu_decode_tiled(
659 const float *x,
660 const float *W_gate,
661 const float *W_up,
662 const float *W_down,
663 const float *b_gate,
664 const float *b_up,
665 const float *b_down,
666 float *output,
667 int D,
668 int Hff);
669
670/* ============================================================================
671 * PREFILL FUSION KERNELS
672 * ============================================================================
673 * These kernels fuse operations for prefill (large batch/sequence) to avoid
674 * writing intermediate activations to DRAM. Fusion helps when activations
675 * exceed L3 cache size.
676 *
677 * For decode (single token), use the non-fused kernels as activations
678 * easily fit in L2 cache anyway.
679 */
680
681/**
682 * @brief Fused RMSNorm + QKV projection for prefill
683 *
684 * Tiles along token dimension to keep intermediate x_norm in L2 cache.
685 * Avoids ~7MB DRAM traffic per layer for seq_len=1024, hidden=896.
686 *
687 * @param scratch Temporary buffer from fused_rmsnorm_qkv_scratch_size()
688 */
689void fused_rmsnorm_qkv_prefill(
690 const float *x, /* [seq_len × hidden] input */
691 const float *gamma, /* [hidden] RMSNorm weights */
692 const float *Wq, /* [q_dim × hidden] Q weights (transposed) */
693 const float *Wk, /* [kv_dim × hidden] K weights (transposed) */
694 const float *Wv, /* [kv_dim × hidden] V weights (transposed) */
695 float *Q, /* [seq_len × q_dim] output */
696 float *K, /* [seq_len × kv_dim] output */
697 float *V, /* [seq_len × kv_dim] output */
698 int seq_len,
699 int hidden,
700 int q_dim,
701 int kv_dim,
702 float eps,
703 float *scratch);
704

706 * @brief Fused RMSNorm + QKV projection for prefill (head-major outputs)

2166// Split a packed recurrent QKV projection into explicit Q, K, and V rows.
2167// Layout:
2168// packed_qkv : [rows, q_dim + k_dim + v_dim] row-major
2169// q : [rows, q_dim]
2170// k : [rows, k_dim]
2171// v : [rows, v_dim]
2172//
2173// For qwen3.5 recurrent layers, rows usually means num_tokens * num_seqs after
2174// the packed projection has been flattened into a token-major matrix.
2175//
2176// Full-attention qwen3.5 layers also use a joint Q+gate projection before the
2177// standard attention block:
2178// packed_qg : [rows, interleaved (q_group, gate_group) segments]
2179// q : [rows, q_dim]
2180// gate : [rows, gate_dim]
2181// group_dim : per-group width; if q_dim == gate_dim == group_dim the layout
2182// degenerates to a single [Q | G] split, otherwise it is treated
2183// as [Q0 | G0 | Q1 | G1 | ...].
2184void split_q_gate_forward(const float *packed_qg,
2185 float *q,
2186 float *gate,
2187 int rows,
2188 int q_dim,
2189 int gate_dim,
2190 int group_dim);

2198 int group_dim);
